info.bio:
There are multiple artists that use the name Shoes.

1) Shoes is an American power pop band that brothers John Murphy and Jeff Murphy alongside Gary Klebe formed in Zion, Illinois in 1974. Picking up a cult following among power pop fans from their mellow, new wave inspired rock. they've incorporated several different drummers over the years, including Barry Shumaker, Skip Meyer, Ric Menck, John Richardson, and Jeff Hunter. The band are perhaps best known for their critically acclaimed albums 'Present Tense' and 'Tongue Twister'

scenes.name: American Graffiti: revival, garage y power-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: American Graffiti (1973) desata el revival de los cincuenta y sesenta, que suenan más auténticos que el rock corporativo de los setenta: rockabilly, surf, folk-rock, psicodelia, bandas sonoras de terror. Los punks descubren el alma malvada del rockabilly: Suicide inventa el psychobilly y los Cramps el «voodoobilly»; Fleshtones, Raybeats, Stray Cats, Von Lmo. El garage revive con Slickee Boys, Pretenders, Wipers, Real Kids; el power-pop con Cheap Trick, Shoes, Cars, Jonathan Richman y Embarrassment. En California, los Blasters y el cow-punk de Rank And File; Tom Petty como teórico del power-pop, Plimsouls, Redd Kross, Go-Go's, Bangles. El blues para la generación punk: George Thorogood, Fabulous Thunderbirds, J. Geils Band, Dixie Dregs.

podcast.title: New Wave Powerpop
podcast.body: The Shoes are mentioned as one of the bands that defined the new wave brand of Powerpop. Their sound reflects the post-punk era, taking the energetic, melodic, and hook-driven characteristics of Powerpop and blending them with new wave sensibilities, showcasing punk's influence. "We had the cars, the shoes, the records, the buzz cocks, Elvis Costello and Joe Jackson."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Cars are identified as one of the new wave bands that embraced Powerpop, integrating its spiky, angular, fun, and sing-along song structures into their sound. They are grouped with other artists who blended punk influences into the Powerpop formula, contributing to its integration into alternative rock. "We had the cars, the shoes, the records, the buzz cocks, Elvis Costello and Joe Jackson."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Records are listed among the artists who contributed to the new wave take on Powerpop. They exemplify the integration of catchy melodies and sharp guitar work with the energy and attitude influenced by punk, marking Powerpop's entry into the alternative rock sphere. "We had the cars, the shoes, the records, the buzz cocks, Elvis Costello and Joe Jackson."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop with Punk Influence
xref.body: The Buzzcocks are cited as a band that incorporated elements of punk into the new wave brand of Powerpop. Their sound, along with contemporaries like Elvis Costello and Joe Jackson, helped define the integration of Powerpop into the alternative rock world. "We had the cars, the shoes, the records, the buzz cocks, Elvis Costello and Joe Jackson."
